gaps.sentence: 'Do you take sugar?' he asked. He asked ___ took sugar.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions take if/whether, not do-support or 'that': asked if I took sugar.

gaps.sentence: 'I have to catch the last train,' she said. She said she ___ catch the last train.
gaps.explanation: Have to (obligation) backshifts to had to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'I must finish this today,' she said. She said she ___ finish it that day.
gaps.explanation: Must expressing obligation usually becomes had to in reported speech; 'today' becomes 'that day'.

gaps.sentence: "Congratulations!" — She ___ me on passing the exam.
'Please, please help me,' the woman begged. The woman begged ___ her.
gaps.explanation: Begging is reported as beg + somebody + to do something.

gaps.sentence: 'You broke my phone!' she said to her brother. She ___ her brother of breaking her phone.
'Watch out for the ice on the road,' she said. She ___ us about the icy road.
gaps.explanation: Warnings about a danger: warn somebody about something (or warn sb to do).

gaps.sentence: 'I'll finish the report today,' she said. She said she would finish the report ___.
gaps.explanation: Today becomes that day when reported later.
